What are some shortcuts you use to learn?

I forgot where I discovered this, but I use this series of questions:

 

Acquire Test - Have I seen/listened to the idea before?

Understand Test - Do I get (at a surface level) what this idea means?

Explore Test - Do I understand where this idea comes from, what it is related to and what outside ideas can be connected with it?

Debug Test - Have I removed inappropriate links between this idea and others? Have I removed false conclusions based on connections that don’t actually exist?

Apply Test - Have I used this idea in my practical life?

It probably depends on what you are trying to learn. I think learning history would be very different than learning calculus.

I spend most of my time learning programming or improving on my guitar playing/song writing. In the case of both music and programming I think the best is to just get your hands dirty and dive right into it and try to make something. When you come across problems that you're facing it's about knowing the right time to back down and isolate the problem and fix it/correct it. I think this concept could be applied to math in the case it's best to just do problems (you'll probably memorize the equations needed much easier if you're using them).

In the case of history or literature, I was never a big fan of that. I'd pretty much try to memorize all that information the night before a test. I'd try and make up little stupid things that would help me. For example (this is a shitty one)... "Hitler is a stickler". I would remember that and go, "He's a bad man!".

If I need to learn something I read it out loud in a weird accent or in english(not my native language).

I also write down, by hand, important parts of a text for example 2-3 times.

It makes it stick somehow.
I do a similar thing where I sing a fact to learn it, lol. I guess it makes it stick out in your mind because it breaks with normal behaviour.
It feels like if you speak out loud in your normal voice it doesn't differentiate from thinking in your own voice. I always learned best when I was in class and listened to the teacher.

I'll echo Puddl3glum and say that reusing Dell's case might not be for the best. Check out Newegg's in-house brand for a case. They are cheap and perform fine.

With that low of a price range you will be better off putting the SSD on the back burner. Build what you can and when you get an unexpected $150 you can always slap one in later. DO YOUR RESEARCH ON THEM FIRST! Several brands have debilitating problems.

Unless you plan to edit videos or do some seriously CPU intensive tasks don't even consider an Intel I7. I may get shit for this but I wouldn't consider any of AMD's CPUs.

Graphics Card wise I'll let someone else suggest something but this is where your budget is going to really show. $600 is a bit cheap for a gaming rig. If you want something to last at least 2 years without an upgrade you'll need at least $800. 1 grand to make it sweet. For your gaming rig the lack of money to spend on a graphics card will be your biggest limitation. But do your homework and don't skimp on anything else and you can easily replace your graphics card at a later time.
